chapter: Los Angeles 1947-48, Rock Island and bebop in New York
title: Collecting his pay, a nervous flight to Chicago
summary: He collected wages outside the bank in fear and flew to Chicago.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: know. But I didn't want to have any parts of the club, not any. Do you blame me? So I got in touch with Charlie. I said, 'Well, I just called Big Sid long distance to send me some money. I'm leaving.' He said, 'Well, man, you didn't have to do that.' He says, 'Tomorrow night's pay night.' And he gave us this night off, you know, ahead of pay night. He says, 'So wait for the banks to open and I'll pay your salary, you know, your week's salary.' So we go to the bank. Ike and I stand outside. By this time he has a patch on his head, taped on. And I had a skitty feeling. 'Ike,' I said, 'do you realize that we could be shot down right here in front of this bank, saying that Charlie's in there holding up the bank and we're lookout men, you know?' I said, 'Let's walk down to the other corner and get away from this bank.' So we walked down to the other corner. Charlie come out, he's looking up and down the street. We said, 'Come on down here where we are.' You know. So he came down and he gave me the money. So then I wished them all adieu and went to the airport. So now, as a rule, businessmen are on there getting their final touches to their business out of their attache case, you know, so everything will be in order when they land. But anytime they see a black, this is like a rabbit's foot. They relax. Everyone's not so attentive to anything that they've got to do. They just put down their reclining seats and go to sleep. The plane's not going to drop with a black man on it. You don't hear of that very often. So I got on the plane and just through

curiosity -- it was sparse with passengers, and I counted them, and I was the 13th one. I'm not superstitious, but at this point I'm expecting anything, everything, and nothing at all. You know, anything can happen. But, we made it to Chicago. So I went to the Pershing Hotel, which is on the South Side, and I woke Sid up. We proceeded to drink. And we must have drank all day. And they've got me telling the story over and over again to everyone that came in the room, you know. And I went to work with him that night. They were working at the Blue Note, downstairs.
